note: Signature codes extracted from the drawing sheets. Per-device grouping is approximate — designators are printed upright and codes rotated, so they come from separate OCR passes. Treat the codes as reliable and the grouping as a hint.
shared: Red Baron uses the same Auxiliary Math Box PCB as Battlezone (Atari 035678-01), so a known-good board from either game checks the other. Device positions read by eye off DP-156 sheet 3 Side B: the six microcode PROMs are M1 (036175), L1 (036176), K1 (036177), J1 (036178), H1 (036179) and F1 (036180); the entry PROM is B1 (036174, 82S123); its address latch is C1 (74LS374); and the ALU is four Atari 137004-001 bit slices at K2, F2, H/J2 and D/E2. An earlier version of this note listed those positions one place out (L1-E1 for the PROMs, J2/F/H2/E2/C/D2 for the slices) -- that came from the approximate OCR grouping described above, and would send you to the wrong chip.
probeNote: Codes marked with an asterisk on the drawing are taken with a 1k resistor between the signature analyser's data probe and +5V. Without it those readings do not reproduce. The note appears only on the 2nd printing of DP-156-03.
